item.title: Brandin Podziemski (GSW): The Warriors will start Brandin Podziemski, Will Richard, De’Anthony Melton, Yaxel Lendeborg, and Draymond Green against the Spurs on Friday.
item.description:
The Warriors will start Brandin Podziemski, Will Richard, De’Anthony Melton, Yaxel Lendeborg, and Draymond Green against the Spurs on Friday.

Steph Curry suffered a right oblique abdominal tear and will be out for tonight’s game. The Warriors made two changes to the starting lineup, first with sliding Draymond Green to the five and replacing Al Horford with Will Richard, and then De’Anthony Melton will start in place of Steph Curry. Richard isn’t a great fantasy player, but Melton is the guy to add if he’s available in your fantasy league.

Brian Taylor De'Anthony Melton Will Richard

item.title: [Recap] Collin Gillespie (PHX): Collin Gillespie provided a boost off the bench with 13 points (5-of-13 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, two steals and three three-pointers on Thursday against the Hornets.
item.description:

item.title: [Recap] Devin Booker (PHX): Devin Booker led the Suns with 30 points (12-of-20 FGs), one rebound, seven assists, three steals, one block and four three-pointers in a 101-96 win over the Hornets on Thursday.
item.description:

After scoring just 17 points in Tuesday’s win, which was a game he only played 29 minutes due to the lopsided score, Booker was able to get back on track in this one. He matched his season high for both steals and three-pointers in the win while also scoring at least 30 points for the fifth time this season. He has been excellent this season and will look to stay hot against the Lakers on Sunday to wrap up the week.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Coby White (CHA): Coby White led the Hornets with 21 points (8-of-16 FGs), three rebounds, three assists and two three-pointers in a 101-96 loss to the Suns on Thursday.
item.description:
Coby White led the Hornets with 21 points (8-of-16 FGs), three rebounds, three assists and two three-pointers in a 101-96 loss to the Suns on Thursday.

It has taken White some time to get going after missing the start of the year, and he’s still on a minutes restriction, but he was able to have his highest scoring performance of the season in this game. Despite playing less than 20 minutes, White led Charlotte in scoring in what was his best game of the season. Hopefully his role will increase as the season progresses, but he is already starting to tick up his production.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Grant Williams (CHA): Grant Williams made his season debut on Thursday and contributed 11 points (3-of-5 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, one block and two three-pointers against the Suns.
item.description:
Grant Williams made his season debut on Thursday and contributed 11 points (3-of-5 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, one block and two three-pointers against the Suns.

Suiting up for the first time this season after missing the start of the year with a hamstring strain, Williams was able to make an impact immediately. Despite playing just 16 minutes, Williams was able to space the floor and score in double figures. They also outscored the Suns by 11 points when he was on the floor, which was the best mark on the team by far. Williams isn’t a standard-league option, but he is a solid depth piece for Charlotte.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Christian Anderson (CHA): Christian Anderson Jr. provided a boost off the bench with 13 points (4-of-9 FGs), two assists and three three-pointers against the Suns on Thursday.
item.description:
Christian Anderson Jr. provided a boost off the bench with 13 points (4-of-9 FGs), two assists and three three-pointers against the Suns on Thursday.

It has been a rough start to Anderson’s career, but he was able to get some offense going in this one. He set a new career high for scoring, and he has knocked down three triples in two straight games. One of the best shooters in the draft, it is good to see Anderson start to get things going on offense. He isn’t worth rostering in redraft leagues, but he is worth stashing in dynasty formats.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Bones Hyland (MIN): Bones Hyland led the Timberwolves with 24 points (7-of-10 FGs), three rebounds, eight assists, two steals and five three-pointers in a 133-94 win over the Mavericks on Thursday.
item.description:
Bones Hyland led the Timberwolves with 24 points (7-of-10 FGs), three rebounds, eight assists, two steals and five three-pointers in a 133-94 win over the Mavericks on Thursday.

Hyland had his best game of the season in what ended up being a blowout win for Minnesota. He set season highs for both points and three-pointers while matching his season high for assists. Hyland has been a solid reserve for the Wolves this season, though the production hasn’t come consistently. Despite a fantastic performance, he isn’t worth adding in most formats due to a limited role.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] LaMelo Ball (MIN): LaMelo Ball lit up the Mavericks with 22 points (8-of-14 FGs), three rebounds, nine assists, two steals and six three-pointers on Thursday.
item.description:
LaMelo Ball lit up the Mavericks with 22 points (8-of-14 FGs), three rebounds, nine assists, two steals and six three-pointers on Thursday.

It wasn’t a monster game for LaMelo, but it didn’t need to be. He made the most of his 25 minutes on the court in the blowout win. This was his fifth straight game with at least 20 points, and he set a new season high for assists. LaMelo took some time to get going, but he is starting to get into a groove with Anthony Edwards sidelined. Minnesota has now won five straight games and will look to extend their streak with the Bulls coming to town on Saturday.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Zaccharie Risacher (DAL): Zaccharie Risacher led the Mavericks with 22 points (9-of-14 FGs), six rebounds, three assists, two steals, one block and four three-pointers in a 133-94 loss to the Timberwolves on Thursday.
item.description:
Zaccharie Risacher led the Mavericks with 22 points (9-of-14 FGs), six rebounds, three assists, two steals, one block and four three-pointers in a 133-94 loss to the Timberwolves on Thursday.

Risacher was the leading scorer for Dallas in this game, though most of his work came after the result had been decided. Risacher had a strong start to the season, specifically on the defensive end. However, he has cooled off a bit in recent weeks, though this was a nice outing for him. However, in the month of November, he has only scored in double figures in the games that were decided by at least 35 points, making him a difficult player to trust in fantasy basketball.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] P.J. Washington (DAL): P.J. Washington finished with 10 points (4-of-7 FGs), three rebounds and one three-pointer against the Timberwolves on Thursday.
item.description:
P.J. Washington finished with 10 points (4-of-7 FGs), three rebounds and one three-pointer against the Timberwolves on Thursday.

Washington got off to a hot start to this game, scoring 10 points in the first quarter. Unfortunately, foul trouble limited him to just 16 minutes, and he didn’t score over the final three quarters. That pretty much sums this game up for Dallas, as they were outscored by 31 points after the first quarter. They were completely dominated in this game, though Washington was able to start off well, so that is something, I suppose. They’ll look to bounce back in Cleveland on Saturday.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Trae Young (WAS): Trae Young led the Wizards with 37 points (8-of-23 FGs, 17-of-17 FTs), two rebounds, 14 assists and four three-pointers in a 144-140 loss to the Pistons in double overtime on Thursday.
item.description:
Trae Young led the Wizards with 37 points (8-of-23 FGs, 17-of-17 FTs), two rebounds, 14 assists and four three-pointers in a 144-140 loss to the Pistons in double overtime on Thursday.

A big fourth quarter led to Trae setting a new season high for scoring. In fact, this was his first 30-point, 10-assist game as a Wizard and the 92nd of his career, which ranks fifth in NBA history. Unfortunately, after scoring his 33rd point at the buzzer with an incredible three-pointer to force overtime, he shot 0-of-7 from the floor in overtime, with the four extra points coming at the free throw line. Still, it was an excellent night for him and was certainly his best performance as a Wizard. It is also worth noting that AJ Dybantsa, despite a rough night, hit a tough mid-range shot to force the second overtime, which was a fun moment for the rookie.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Alex Caruso (OKC): Alex Caruso accounted for 14 points (4-of-6 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, three steals and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
item.description:
Alex Caruso accounted for 14 points (4-of-6 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, three steals and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.

The Thunder didn’t have Ajay Mitchell for Wednesday’s game, opening a spot in the starting lineup for Caruso. He took advantage of the opportunity, shooting 4-of-5 from beyond the arc. Caruso’s 14 points were a new season high for him, as he totaled 17 points in the first four games he played upon returning from an ankle injury. If Mitchell remains out for Friday’s game against the Clippers, Caruso would be worth rostering in 14-team leagues and some 12-team leagues.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Isaiah Hartenstein (OKC): Isaiah Hartenstein accumulated 20 points (10-of-14 FGs), 11 rebounds, six assists and two steals in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
item.description:
Isaiah Hartenstein accumulated 20 points (10-of-14 FGs), 11 rebounds, six assists and two steals in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.

After totaling 19 points in Oklahoma City’s first five games of November, Hartenstein recorded his first 20-point game of the season on Wednesday. The negative for iHart was the turnovers, of which he was responsible for six. A few of the turnovers were due to offensive fouls, so there isn’t much to worry about there. Rostered in 83 percent of Yahoo leagues, Hartenstein is providing top-100 fantasy value, slightly better than his ADP.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (OKC): Shai Gilgeous-Alexander produced 31 points (9-of-20 FGs, 13-of-14 FTs), four rebounds, two assists and one steal in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
item.description:
Shai Gilgeous-Alexander produced 31 points (9-of-20 FGs, 13-of-14 FTs), four rebounds, two assists and one steal in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.

Gilgeous-Alexander has scored at least 30 points in six games this season. Unfortunately for him and the Thunder, the team’s lack of established scorers proved costly in both losses to the Trail Blazers. Five other Thunder players scored in double figures, with Isaiah Hartenstein’s 20 leading the way. The lack of creators who can take some of the pressure off of Gilgeous-Alexander was evident in both losses to the Trail Blazers. He’ll remain an elite fantasy option, but SGA’s ceiling may have taken a slight hit because a few of his teammates are injured.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Jrue Holiday (POR): Jrue Holiday accumulated 19 points (5-of-12 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, two steals and five three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.
item.description:
Jrue Holiday accumulated 19 points (5-of-12 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, two steals and five three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.

A double-digit scorer in seven straight games, Holiday provided solid fantasy value on Wednesday. In addition to the 19 points, he shot 5-of-8 from beyond the arc and recorded good numbers in assists and steals. Through 11 games, Holiday has been close to a top-100 fantasy player, something most managers did not expect before the season began.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Sidy Cissoko (POR): Sidy Cissoko produced 19 points (6-of-9 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), two rebounds and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.
item.description:
Sidy Cissoko produced 19 points (6-of-9 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), two rebounds and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.

Replacing Scoot Henderson (5/2/2 with one three-pointer) in the starting lineup ahead of Tuesday’s win over the Thunder, Cissoko played well in both victories. The Trail Blazers wing totaled 36 points, five rebounds, three assists, one steal and seven three-pointers in Portland’s two-game sweep of Oklahoma City. While Cissoko isn’t a must-add player right now, he’s worth watching in deep leagues to see if the last two games were a fluke.

item.title: [Recap] Damian Lillard (POR): Damian Lillard recorded 18 points (5-of-14 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.
item.description:
Damian Lillard recorded 18 points (5-of-14 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.

item.title: [Recap] Deni Avdija (POR): Deni Avdija tallied 28 points (9-of-20 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, six assists, four steals, two blocks and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.
item.description:
Deni Avdija tallied 28 points (9-of-20 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, six assists, four steals, two blocks and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.

One night removed from scoring 24 points in a win over the Thunder, Avdija was just as productive in the rematch. The 28 points were the most he’s scored in a game since November 2, when the Trail Blazers forward hit that number in a win over the Nuggets. While there were questions before the season began about Portland’s offensive pecking order, there haven’t been any issues so far, even when the currently injured Ja Morant was healthy. item.description:

Mitchell has scored in double figures in five straight and nine of his last 10 games. Injuries that have beset the Thunder this season have created more opportunities for the third-year guard, who is averaging a career-high 18.5 points per game and providing top-100 fantasy value. As long as Mitchell stays healthy, he’s capable of maintaining his current production all season long.

item.title: [Recap] Jared McCain (OKC): Jared McCain tallied 21 points (6-of-12 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, three assists and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
item.description:

After scoring 19 points off the bench in Saturday’s rout of the Wizards, McCain returned to the Thunder starting lineup on Tuesday. Shooting 4-of-7 from beyond the arc, the third-year guard recorded his third 20-point stat line of the season. While he can be inconsistent, McCain is on a bit of a heater, scoring 21, 19 and 21 points in his last three games.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (OKC): Shai Gilgeous-Alexander recorded 26 points (8-of-22 FGs, 10-of-11 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists and one block in Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
item.description:
Shai Gilgeous-Alexander recorded 26 points (8-of-22 FGs, 10-of-11 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists and one block in Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.

After playing the entire third quarter, Gilgeous-Alexander did not play at all in the fourth, as Portland managed to pull away. Due to Oklahoma City’s many injuries, the two-time MVP is being asked to do even more heavy lifting on offense. SGA’s field-goal percentage suffered on Tuesday, but that doesn’t do much to change his status as one of the most valuable players to roster in fantasy basketball. Oklahoma City plays Portland again on Wednesday, and the extra rest time he picked up in the fourth quarter on Tuesday could pay dividends for SGA.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Sidy Cissoko (POR): Sidy Cissoko recorded 17 points (5-of-14 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Thunder.
item.description:
Sidy Cissoko recorded 17 points (5-of-14 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Thunder.

Trail Blazers head coach Micah Nori made a change to his starting lineup on Tuesday, replacing Scoot Henderson with Cissoko. While he didn’t shoot well from the field, Sidy finished with a season-high point total and a solid overall stat line in 33 minutes. Henderson played 23 minutes and finished with 11 points, one rebound, four assists and three three-pointers. Cissoko isn’t a must-add, but he’s worth watching, especially with Ja Morant (hamstring) out for a few more weeks.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Deni Avdija (POR): Deni Avdija finished Tuesday’s win over the Thunder with 24 points (8-of-15 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), six rebounds, eight assists, one steal and two three-pointers.
item.description:
Deni Avdija finished Tuesday’s win over the Thunder with 24 points (8-of-15 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), six rebounds, eight assists, one steal and two three-pointers.

Avdija and Damian Lillard took over the third quarter of Tuesday’s 123-103 victory, combining to score 22 of the Trail Blazers’ 38 points. The former supplemented his nine points with three rebounds and three assists in the period, and Deni has scored at least 21 points in eight of Portland’s 10 games. The two teams meet again on Wednesday in what could be another big night for Avdija, who finished Tuesday’s win two assists shy of a double-double.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Damian Lillard (POR): Damian Lillard amassed 25 points (8-of-15 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Thunder.
item.description:
Damian Lillard amassed 25 points (8-of-15 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Thunder.

Fans got to see “vintage Dame” during the third quarter, with his production helping Portland grab control of the season. Shooting 5-of-6 from the field, Lillard scored 13 points in the third. The final three points came on a 35-footer as time expired, giving Portland a 17-point lead heading into the fourth quarter. Lillard didn’t play in the fourth quarter, and the 24 minutes he did play may ensure he’s available for Wednesday’s rematch.

item.description:
Luka Dončić accumulated 32 points (11-of-22 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), eight rebounds, 10 assists, five steals and two blocks over 39 minutes to lead the Lakers to a 124-114 win over the Hawks on Monday.

Dončić fell short of the 40-point plateau in his return from a one-game absence due to a minor back issue, but showed no signs of rust, turning in another spectacular all-around performance that left him two rebounds shy of a triple-double. He scored 18 of his 32 points after halftime, helping Los Angeles withstand a late Atlanta rally before pulling away in the closing minutes. The Lakers were also without Austin Reaves (illness) in this one, making Dončić’s latest all-around performance even more impressive. The 27-year-old franchise cornerstone has been virtually unstoppable through the early stages of the season and has quickly established himself as the frontrunner in the MVP race.
